features.reason: Archive, Mini and THE END repeat stable source/coverage responsibilities with different color designs. Font/file/worker/saved-run owners have different lifetimes; reuse the dedicated synchronous RGB surface.

contract.input: React hooks, AbsoluteFill, stable Source/children, template id prefix, enabled flag and a synchronous SVG callback from colorInput to colorOutput. Caller owns numeric defaults and RGB design.
contract.output: A stable source tree; optional sRGB pointwise RGB grade with original coverage.
contract.identity: One stable per-mounted-instance document filter identity, independent of settings or independently compiled program copies. React useId, with crypto.getRandomValues per-mount fallback for older React callers.
contract.dependencies: React createElement and Remotion AbsoluteFill; browser Filter Effects color-matrix, transfer and compositing semantics. No SDK/IPC. React useId/useMemo and browser crypto.getRandomValues on the older-React fallback.
contract.effects: DOM and SVG rendering only, no files, network, timers or global mutable state.
contract.lifetime: The source stays in the same inner container across enabled/disabled edits; the color graph can change synchronously.
contract.cleanup: React removes the source once when the real owner unmounts/replaces it. No media, installed assets or foreign runtime cleanup.
contract.outcomes: Every source alpha is retained and the RGB grade is independent of translucency. Color-only contract excludes grain/leak/blur/intentional coverage-changing overlays.
contract.retry: Render changes are repeatable. Deliberate Source replacement still retires the previous component; persistence remains under the existing authoring/run owner.
contract.distribution: Canonical shared/render-color-filter.js is generated into explicitly shipped Archive, Mini and THE END TSX assets via panel-modules.json.
contract.validation: 34 actual component/SVG checks: lifetime, distinct/stable ids with/without useId, frozen original Chromium opaque baseline, 256 alphas and eight colors. Final real Electron evidence is in docs/template-repair/render-color-filter.md. Whole-template acceptance remains open.

findings.title: An analyzed own track can change or disappear before another Build.
findings.mechanism: Own-grid state is retained by a path and UI generation, without a complete file identity carried into the assembly/recovery request. A valid 30-second 120-BPM WAV replaced by an equal-size/equal-mtime 100-BPM WAV still gives the second actual Build planner 119.99 BPM; removing the track also reaches the assembly dispatch boundary.
findings.acceptance: Use the existing asset/input owners to bind own-track analysis and persisted Audio to confirmed bytes through Build, commit and recovery. Preserve the same original plan or reject changed/missing/unknown input; test unchanged reuse, replacement, cancellation and saved-look restoration. Extract the identical numerical engine with parity rather than add another file/cache owner.
findings.resolution: Reuse existing source, asset, Worker and durable owners: analyze a verified snapshot, bind the grid to full original contents, recheck before import/dispatch/commit and on saved-look continuation, and validate the actual Audio path and planned minimum duration. The four identical engines now share one canonical CJS source.
findings.validationLimits: Source/real-media fixtures prove admission and saved-Audio restoration. Native decoder/Worker proof is a separate development checkpoint; installed UI, real Project save/playback/export, released builds and Windows remain open.

findings.title: The own-track duration fallback hides terminal native media uncertainty.
findings.mechanism: hostProbeSeconds catches every runAssetMediaTool error and returns null. Its fallback caller therefore cannot distinguish a known failed probe from an unconfirmed native process exit, even though the shared client now propagates that distinction.
findings.acceptance: Add an actual-adapter counterexample. Preserve ordinary optional probe fallback while propagating terminal/unknown lifetime into a state that cannot be treated as a usable music selection. Keep cancellation and current generation behavior.
findings.resolution: The Mini native duration adapter propagates terminal and preserveTemporaryFiles failures. Ordinary optional probe failure remains null; the snapshot analysis adapter alone decides fallback and selection clears on source/lifetime uncertainty.
findings.validationLimits: Actual adapter terminal/preserve and ordinary-failure controls pass in fixtures; production/Windows proof remains open.

findings.title: Package preparation/compatibility text understates mandatory original-video checks.
findings.mechanism: The manifest still describes native fingerprint as a local-unanalysed-video requirement and asks for analyzed videos. Current code admits every selected video through fingerprint and supports analysis-optional input. INSTALL still promises a broad fallback when host functions are missing.
findings.acceptance: Align declared inputs/capabilities with actual admission and distinguish missing source-confirmation capabilities from ordinary decoder fallback. Retain explicit unverified released-version/Windows status; do not infer compatibility from wording.
findings.resolution: Manifest and INSTALL now require complete native identities for all selected video originals and music. Analysis is optional; decoder fallback never bypasses source confirmation. Storage/cache and unknown-workspace behavior are documented.
findings.validationLimits: Declared contract reconciled to the current source and regression behavior; this wording does not prove released-version, installed-root or Windows compatibility.

findings.title: Configured installation-root compatibility needs a reproduced host contract.
findings.mechanism: INSTALL describes environment-provided panels/skills roots while Mini derives them from the SDK host home. Additional tracing found that the current host installer derives those same paths and exports them to shell children; their scratch HOME is separate. Real-source in-memory composition agrees for macOS, Windows drive and UNC homes. An arbitrary-root override or actual failing installation was not established; this is not a confirmed source mismatch.
findings.acceptance: Identify a supported host/version with a reproducible installation-root mismatch before designing a change. Preserve current installer/SDK-home behavior; verify released/native Windows contracts separately. Do not introduce a roots API or change lookup solely to resolve an unproven defect.

findings.title: Color grades preserve original alpha and source lifetime across strength zero.
findings.mechanism: Arithmetic additions multiplied premultiplied alpha/RGB; the zero-strength branch moved Source to a different React tree position.
findings.acceptance: All source coverage retained, independent RGB grade, normal opaque samples unchanged, zero toggles retain the original and real owner unmount/replacement cleans once.
findings.remaining: Installed full-app, saved Draft, whole-video/audio playback, encoded export and Windows acceptance remain open.
findings.resolution: The common useColorFilter keeps fixed source slots, opaque RGB input, final original-alpha coverage, and unique stable per-mount identities. The three template designs retain their original math.
findings.validationLimits: Unit/standard-model and isolated Chromium evidence only; installed app, whole-video/audio playback, encoded export, Windows and overall template acceptance remain open.

findings.title: Shared file helpers have one source without conflating distinct media policies.
findings.mechanism: A whole copied av-host equality check coupled another app to Archive media adapters despite different dependencies and execution policies.
findings.acceptance: Canonical shared helpers match across declared consumers; adapters retain behavior and complete emitted runtime stays unchanged.
findings.resolution: Extract common facade only, keep media owners, enforce strict canonical boundary checks and real adapter tests.
findings.validationLimits: Source/unit adapter compatibility; installed app, save/playback/export and Windows acceptance remain open.

findings.title: Missing translation keys inherited JavaScript prototype entries and returned empty labels.
findings.mechanism: constructor, toString and __proto__ are absent from STRINGS but ordinary indexed lookup still reads their inherited values. t returns an empty message and tOr bypasses its supplied fallback. Missing interpolation variables could also read inherited constructor/toString values instead of preserving placeholders.
findings.acceptance: Only registered own dictionary messages resolve; missing keys preserve the key or caller fallback, while explicit own messages, existing translation forms and template isolation retain behavior.
findings.resolution: One canonical runtime checks own dictionary entries for both locale/English lookup and optional-key admission. All seven original implementations reproduce the failure.
findings.validationLimits: Actual-source translation calls and compiled runtime/legacy checks; no claimed installed UI symptom, full playback/export or Windows acceptance.
